name: EIA Hourly Electric Grid Monitor (Form EIA-930)
summary: Hourly demand, day-ahead demand forecast, net generation by fuel and interchange for US balancing authorities. Bulk download and API.

name: EIA-860 Annual Electric Generator Report
summary: Generator-level data for US plants of 1 MW and above: location, capacity, technology, status, planned additions and retirements.

name: EIA-861 Annual Electric Power Industry Report
summary: Utility-level sales, customers, revenue, demand response program enrollment and distributed generation by US utility.

name: PUDL (Public Utility Data Liberation), Catalyst Cooperative
summary: Cleaned and linked EIA, FERC and EPA data in SQLite and Parquet. Removes most of the cleanup work of using raw EIA/FERC files.

name: LBNL Queued Up: interconnection queue data
summary: 2026 edition: generation and storage requests through end-2025 from 7 ISOs and 50 other areas; XLSX with codebook, CC BY 4.0. Median request-to-operation over 5 years; 13% of 2000 to 2020 requests reached operation. Excludes load requests.

name: Interconnection.fyi
summary: Searchable aggregation of US interconnection queue projects by ISO, utility, county and point of interconnection.

name: PJM Data Miner 2
summary: PJM load, load forecast, LMP prices, generation and reserve data. API needs a free key.

name: CAISO OASIS
summary: CAISO prices, load, forecasts, transmission and ancillary service data. Queryable by URL API.

name: ERCOT data products
summary: ERCOT load, prices, generation and system reports. ERCOT also publishes large load interconnection status reports.

name: SCE Distribution Resources Plan External Portal (DRPEP)
summary: Southern California Edison feeder-level integration (hosting) capacity maps and grid data. Example of a utility hosting capacity portal.

name: PG&E Grid Resource Integration Portal (GRIP)
summary: PG&E data for California: feeder and line-section load and generation hosting capacity (ICA), forecasts, grid needs, substations and lines, with map exports and a no-login REST service. PG&E says values are directional, not a guarantee. Older DRP page: pge.com distributed-resource-planning-data-and-maps.

name: Open Infrastructure Map
summary: Map of OpenStreetMap power lines, substations, power plants and telecom infrastructure. Underlying data via OSM / Overpass.

name: FCC National Broadband Map
summary: Provider-reported fixed and mobile broadband availability by location (CSV and GIS). Not fiber routes, capacity or latency. Download page blocks scripts.

name: PeeringDB
summary: Database of colocation facilities, exchanges and networks with coordinates and a public API (peeringdb.com/apidocs). Facility records include diverse_serving_substations, a declared field, not measured capacity.

name: PNNL IM3 Open Source Data Center Atlas
summary: Open geospatial inventory of existing US data center locations compiled by Pacific Northwest National Laboratory.

name: Epoch AI data on AI data centers
summary: Tracked large AI data center projects with estimated power, compute and timelines. Focused on large sites, not edge.

name: US Census American Community Survey
summary: ACS 5-year estimates via API down to block group. All Census API queries now need a free key.

name: WRI Aqueduct water risk atlas
summary: Global water stress and water risk indicators by watershed. Relevant to cooling water availability.

name: EPA eGRID
summary: Emissions and generation mix for US power plants and grid subregions. Annual average emission rates.

name: OpenEI Utility Rate Database
summary: US retail electricity tariffs including energy charges, demand charges and time-of-use periods. API available.

name: National Solar Radiation Database (NSRDB)
summary: Gridded hourly and sub-hourly solar irradiance and weather. Used to model on-site solar output at a location.

name: Google cluster workload traces
summary: Borg traces: 2019 (eight cells, May 2019) and 2011 (one ~12,500-machine cell), plus power traces for 57 power domains in May 2019. CC BY.

name: Azure Public Dataset
summary: Azure VM, serverless function and LLM inference request traces. The inference traces show request timing and token counts.

name: Alibaba cluster traces
summary: Production traces 2017 to 2026, including GPU traces (2020, 2023, 2025, 2026 up to 155k GPUs), LLM serving and spot GPU. Some downloads need a survey; license per release.

name: Materials Project
summary: DFT-computed properties for 150k+ inorganic materials: formation energy, band gap, stability, battery electrode data. Free API key.

name: Open Quantum Materials Database (OQMD)
summary: DFT formation energies and structures for about 1M materials. Downloadable database and REST API.

name: JARVIS (NIST)
summary: NIST DFT, force-field and ML datasets and tools for materials, including 2D materials and solar-relevant properties.

name: AFLOW
summary: High-throughput DFT database of millions of material entries with REST API.

name: Alexandria materials database
summary: Millions of DFT calculations of periodic compounds, used to train ML interatomic potentials.

name: OMat24 (Meta FAIR)
summary: About 110M DFT single-point calculations on inorganic structures, released for training ML potentials.

name: Open Catalyst Project (OC20, OC22)
summary: Large DFT datasets of adsorbate-catalyst relaxations for renewable energy reactions, with leaderboards.

name: GNoME materials discovery data (Google DeepMind)
summary: Predicted stable crystal structures from the GNoME project (Nature 2023), with released structures and models.

name: Catalysis-Hub
summary: Surface reaction energies and barriers from DFT, searchable with GraphQL API.

name: Battery cycle life dataset (Severson et al. 2019), data.matr.io
summary: 124 LFP/graphite cells cycled to failure under fast-charge protocols. Standard benchmark for early cycle-life prediction.

name: Battery Archive
summary: Repository of battery cycling data from multiple labs in a common format.

name: NASA Prognostics Center of Excellence data sets
summary: Run-to-failure datasets including Li-ion battery aging data used for prognostics research.

name: NREL (now NLR) Best Research-Cell Efficiency Chart
summary: Record confirmed efficiencies of research solar cells by technology since 1976.

name: The Perovskite Database
summary: Device data from 40k+ perovskite solar cells extracted from the literature: composition, architecture, efficiency, stability.

name: Open Power System Data
summary: Cleaned European time series (load, wind, solar, prices), power plant lists and weather data.

name: NREL (now NLR) ComStock
summary: Simulated hourly end-use load profiles for the US commercial building stock.

name: NREL (now NLR) ResStock
summary: Simulated hourly end-use load profiles for the US residential building stock.

name: Building Data Genome Project 2
summary: Two years of hourly meter data from 1,636 non-residential buildings with weather and metadata. Used for load forecasting benchmarks.

name: ERA5 reanalysis (Copernicus)
summary: Global hourly weather reanalysis from 1940. Common input for load, wind and solar forecasting.

name: NREL (now NLR) WIND Toolkit
summary: Modeled wind speed and power for 126k US sites at 5-minute resolution, 2007 to 2013.

name: FAIR-MAST (UKAEA MAST tokamak data)
summary: Open diagnostic data from the MAST spherical tokamak, released by UKAEA with an API and cloud-native formats.

name: The Well (Polymathic AI)
summary: 15 TB collection of physics simulations, including magnetohydrodynamics, for training and benchmarking surrogate models.

name: Texas A&M Electric Grid Test Case Repository
summary: Synthetic power system cases from 200 to 70,000 buses (Illinois, South Carolina, Texas, western, northeastern and eastern US) in MATPOWER, PSS/E, PowerWorld and PSLF formats. Free for commercial and non-commercial use. Not real utility networks.

name: ACTIVSg10k: 10,000-bus synthetic grid, western US
summary: Synthetic grid on the US WECC footprint, 16 areas. Package includes a MATPOWER case, substation latitude/longitude in the PowerWorld .aux file, and an N-1 branch contingency list. No hourly load time series. Also bundled with MATPOWER as case_ACTIVSg10k.

name: ACTIVSg2000: 2,000-bus synthetic grid, Texas
summary: Synthetic grid on the ERCOT footprint. Package includes a MATPOWER case, contingencies and a year of hourly load scenarios. Also bundled with MATPOWER as case_ACTIVSg2000.

name: Overpass API (OpenStreetMap queries)
creator: OpenStreetMap community (Roland Olbricht)
summary: Query OpenStreetMap features by tag and area, e.g. power=substation, power=line with voltage, building footprints. No key; public endpoints are rate-limited. OSM coverage of grid assets is volunteer-mapped and uneven.

name: Microsoft US Building Footprints
summary: Building footprint polygons for the US derived from imagery, by state, GeoJSON. ODbL license.

name: Census Reporter API
creator: Census Reporter
summary: Simplified access to ACS tables by geography through api.censusreporter.org. No key, unlike the official Census API.

name: CPUC High Fire Threat District map
summary: California fire threat tiers (Tier 2 elevated, Tier 3 extreme) used for utility fire safety rules, published as a map and ArcGIS feature service.

name: Open-Meteo weather API
creator: Open-Meteo (Patrick Zippenfenig)
summary: Weather forecasts and historical reanalysis by coordinate, hourly, JSON. No key for non-commercial use.

name: ESA WorldCover
summary: Global 10 m land cover maps for 2020 and 2021 from Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2.

name: EAGLE-I recorded electricity outages 2014 to 2022 (ORNL)
summary: Customers without power by US county at 15-minute intervals, 2014 to 2022, from DOE's EAGLE-I system. Live EAGLE-I portal: eagle-i.doe.gov.

name: ACN-Data: EV charging sessions (Caltech)
summary: Real EV charging sessions from Caltech, JPL and an office site: arrival, departure, energy requested and delivered. API with a free token.

name: AFDC alternative fuel station locator (US DOE)
summary: US public EV charging stations with location, network, connector types and power level. API through the NREL developer network (free key).

name: Grid Status (gridstatus.io): live and historical data for all US ISOs
creator: Grid Status
summary: Web dashboards and API with live and historical prices (LMP), demand, forecasts and fuel mix across US ISOs: CAISO, ERCOT, PJM, MISO, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE. Browse in the browser; an account is needed for the API and downloads. Python library: gridstatus.

name: Starter data: US grid demand and generation, hourly, 2025 (12 operators)
creator: Built for this repo from US EIA-930
summary: Ready-to-load CSV: hourly 2025 demand, day-ahead forecast, net generation, interchange and generation by fuel (coal, gas, nuclear, hydro, solar, wind, battery and more) for CAISO, ERCOT, PJM, MISO, NYISO, ISO-NE, SPP, BPA, Duke, Southern, TVA, FPL. Plus an annual summary file. One-line pandas loader in the README.

name: LBNL, United States Data Center Energy Usage Report: 2025 Update
summary: Estimates US data center use at 521 to 843 TWh in 2030, 9.5% to 15.3% of US electricity, central estimate 11.8%.

name: IEA, Key Questions on Energy and AI (2026)
summary: Data center demand grew 17% in 2025 (AI-focused 50%); 485 TWh in 2025 to about 950 TWh in 2030. Projects 20 to 25 GW batteries and 15 to 27 GW onsite gas at data centers by 2030. CC BY 4.0.

name: EIA, Data center server energy use grows across the commercial building stock (AEO2026)
summary: AEO2026 models data center server electricity separately and uses an essentially flat server load shape.

name: EIA, Annual Energy Outlook 2026 narrative
summary: High Electricity Demand case with more AI servers; high-case server consumption reaches 818 TWh in 2050.

name: DOE, Electricity Demand Growth Resource Hub
summary: Federal hub of analyses, programs and resources on rapid load growth, including data centers.

name: DOE, Powering America's AI Future: Data Center Resource Hub
summary: Federal hub on data center demand, flexibility, efficiency, grid integration, water and DOE programs.

name: DOE, Microgrids, Large Electric Loads and Grid Support
summary: US data center use rose from 58 TWh (2014) to 176 TWh (2023), 325 to 580 TWh possible by 2028; covers storage, CHP and microgrids for large loads.

name: Virginia JLARC, Data Centers in Virginia (2024)
summary: State investigation: 250+ interviews, independent demand forecast, E3 grid cost modeling. About 50 ongoing jobs vs 1,500 at construction peak for a 250k sq ft site; low-frequency noise; $14 to $37/month added residential cost by 2040 (modeled).

name: Commercial mobile edge computing market forecast (press release, 2026)
summary: Vendor forecast: USD 0.80B (2025) to 3.88B (2031), 30.1% CAGR. Methodology not inspected; measures mobile edge computing, not edge data center buildings or MW.

name: ETSI White Paper 55, MEC support towards edge-native design (2023)
summary: Edge constraints: limited single-rack resources, heterogeneity, intermittent upstream links, user mobility, latency. Covers MEC 021 application mobility and MEC 011 discovery APIs.

name: ETSI, Multi-access Edge Computing security white paper (2022)
summary: Scope of edge security across federation, physical, data, network and application layers in multi-vendor edge ecosystems. Announcement only; full paper linked.

name: ETSI MEC technical group
summary: Defines multi-access edge computing as cloud capabilities and an IT service environment at the network edge.

name: California Energy Commission, Data Centers
summary: CEC does not generally permit data centers but forecasts their demand. Early 2026 data centers were about 1,000 MW, roughly 2% of CAISO peak.

name: City of Santa Clara, data center zoning framework
summary: 2024 zoning code requires standalone data centers to obtain a Conditional Use Permit and architectural review.

name: City of Santa Clara, Planning Commission data center record
summary: Review of noise, fiscal benefits, power use and concentration of data centers; CUP required in Office/R&D and industrial districts.

name: San Francisco Planning, code change summaries and interim controls
summary: Index of adopted and interim controls, including an interim zoning moratorium for data centers in San Francisco.

name: San Francisco Property Information Map
summary: Parcel reports: zoning, height/bulk, overlays, permits, hazards (flooding, sea-level rise, liquefaction), year built. Not structural or electrical capacity.

name: Prince William County, data center overlay district review
summary: Specified new data center proposals now go through special-use-permit review instead of by-right zoning.

name: Loudoun County, Data Centers: Land Use Considerations
summary: Rural policy area zoning, about two-thirds of county land, does not allow data centers.

name: Loudoun County, Data Center Standards and Locations
summary: Phase 1 (approved 18 Mar 2025) moved data centers from by-right to Special Exception in affected areas. Phase 2 (plan approved 16 Sep 2025) covers data center and substation standards. Includes existing/proposed data center map.

name: Tulare County, temporary moratorium on new data centers (CEQAnet)
summary: Moratorium extension while the county develops zoning, infrastructure, water, energy, noise and safety standards.

name: City of Richmond CA, temporary moratorium on new data centers (CEQAnet)
summary: Citywide moratorium extended through 15 Sep 2028 while permanent rules are evaluated.

name: Virginia DEQ, issued air permits for data centers
summary: List of air permits for data center backup generation: facility, locality, permit ID, dates.

name: National Zoning Atlas
summary: Standardized zoning for 11,000+ jurisdictions, 200+ characteristics per district. Data center is not a normalized permitted-use field.

name: LBNL, The water use of data center workloads (2025)
summary: Workload-level water use varies by more than four orders of magnitude with server efficiency, grid water factors, cooling, climate and utilization.

name: JRC, 2024 EU Code of Conduct for Data Centres best practice guidelines
summary: Catalogue of data center practices (cooling, airflow, waste heat, geography, water, monitoring) with 1 to 5 qualitative values that must not be summed. CC BY 4.0.

name: Census TIGER/Line shapefiles (2026)
summary: National boundaries, roads, rails, hydrography; 2026 release 14 Oct 2026. Not parcels or zoning.

name: NOAA Climate Data Online API v2
summary: Station observations and climate normals as JSON. Token header; 5 requests/s, 10,000/day; max 1,000 results per call.

name: USGS Water Data APIs
summary: REST/OGC APIs for streamflow, groundwater, daily and continuous values at 1M+ monitoring sites. Not a water right or utility allocation.

name: MRLC Annual National Land Cover Database
summary: Annual US land cover, change and imperviousness 1985 to 2025 (Collection 1.2, June 2026). Downloads and WMS.

name: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer
summary: Effective flood maps covering 90%+ of US population, via viewer, downloads and GIS services. Unmapped does not mean no flood risk.

name: FEMA National Risk Index (OpenFEMA)
summary: v1.20 (Dec 2025): risk for 18 hazards by state, county, tract. Tables, shapefiles, geodatabases, 39 to 411 MB. Old hazards.fema.gov/nri URL redirects.

name: RIPE Atlas public measurements (BigQuery)
summary: Ping, traceroute, DNS, HTTP measurements from deployed probes since 2020, queryable in BigQuery (Google account). Measured latency between probes and targets, not arbitrary sites.

name: PG&E GRIP user guide and quick start (REST endpoint)
summary: Documents PG&E load ICA: 576 hourly results per line section for four limiting criteria, feeder CSV/ZIP downloads, no-login ArcGIS REST at services2.arcgis.com/mJaJSax0KPHoCNB6/arcgis/rest/services/DRPComplianceRelProd/FeatureServer. Values are directional, not a guarantee.

name: PG&E GIS Data Hub
summary: Selected PG&E infrastructure and risk GIS layers as ArcGIS services.

name: SCE ICA ArcGIS FeatureServer
summary: Machine-readable SCE integration capacity layers. Tables at .../hosted/ICA_Tables/FeatureServer.

name: SDG&E Integration Capacity Analysis
summary: Distribution ICA map for SDG&E territory; 2025 update added Limited Generation Profile data.

name: CAISO 2027 Local Capacity Requirements
summary: Local reliability studies and capacity requirements for constrained California transmission areas.

name: CAISO Today's Outlook
summary: Near-real-time CAISO demand, supply, renewables and emissions dashboards with CSV downloads.

name: CAISO Resource Adequacy
summary: RA program pages and aggregate capacity files for the CAISO balancing area.

name: ERCOT, Interconnection and Grid Analysis Update (Apr 2026)
summary: As of 26 Mar 2026, data centers were 87.6% of MW in ERCOT's large-load request portfolio.

name: ERCOT, 2025 Report on Existing and Potential Electric System Constraints and Needs
summary: 238.6 GW of large-load requests vs 7,502 MW approved to energize since Jan 2022. Unadjusted 2031 TSP forecast 218 GW vs studied 159 GW. $30.21B transmission planned 2026 to 2031.

name: ERCOT, Large Load update to Texas legislature (Apr 2026)
summary: About 410 GW of large-load requests (about 87% data centers) as of 26 Mar 2026. Explains batch studies about every six months; proposed $50,000/MW security fee.

name: ERCOT / PUCT, Batch Zero process for large loads (Jun 2026)
summary: PUCT approved ERCOT's batch study process to decide how much large load ERCOT can reliably connect and where.

name: ERCOT NPRR1234, large load interconnection requirements
summary: Interconnection and modeling requirements for loads of 25 MW or more.

name: ERCOT market notice, large electronic load ride-through (Jun 2025)
summary: ERCOT asked data center and crypto loads of 75 MW+ for voltage ride-through data because simultaneous trips threaten reliability.

name: ERCOT Emergency Response Service (ERS)
summary: Loads, generators and aggregations paid to reduce consumption within 10 or 30 minutes during energy emergencies. Procured four times a year via QSEs. ERCOT is not under FERC Order 2222.

name: PJM, 2025 Long-Term Load Forecast Report
summary: 20-year zonal peak and energy forecast with data center adjustments in 10 zones. Summer peak +3.1%/yr, 209,923 MW by 2035. Tables in Excel.

name: PJM, 2026 Long-Term Load Forecast
summary: 10-year average growth 3.6%/yr summer peak, 4.0%/yr winter peak; data center adjustments a major component.

name: PJM, 2025 Year in Review: Planning
summary: Vetted data center load projected to grow about 30 GW from 2025 to 2030.

name: PJM, annual vetting of large load requests (Sep 2026)
summary: PJM has no load interconnection queue; load-serving entities submit large-load adjustments to the forecast, which PJM vets.

name: NOVEC data center forecast documentation (PJM 2026 forecast)
summary: Bottom-up utility method: contract milestones, site control, zoning; moderate-risk projects discounted 50%. July peak 1,387 MW (2025) to 5,032 MW (2030) forecast.

name: PJM / Dominion review of large load transfer event (Aug 2026)
summary: Nearly 4,000 MW of data center load disconnected unexpectedly in Virginia on 22 Jul 2026; earlier events were about 1,500 MW.

name: PJM, proposed reliability standards for large load disconnection (Sep 2026)
summary: Proposed requirements for computational loads after the July 2026 event and a June 2026 FERC directive. Proposal, not effective rule.

name: PJM Data Miner, seven-day load forecast feed
summary: Hourly forecast MW by area with evaluation time and target time, so lead time is separable. API needs a PJM account.

name: PJM Data Miner, historical load forecasts feed
summary: Every forecast vintage since 1 Jan 2011, created every six hours. Pair with actual load to measure forecast error.

name: MISO, Large Load Additions framework
summary: Requests seek connection in 18 to 36 months. Goal of approval within 120 days. Mechanisms include non-firm service, firm-service step-up, curtailment, telemetry, ride-through.

name: MISO, Firm Service Step Up for large load interconnections
summary: Proposed process letting large loads start with reduced firm service before all upgrades are complete.

name: MISO, large load telemetry and PMU requirements
summary: Draft: real-time large load telemetry over ICCP and PMU measurements at the point of interconnection.

name: MISO, Generation and Large Load Alignment (LLWG-2026-6)
summary: Proposal to study large loads together with the generation serving them. Under development.

name: MISO, Expedited Resource Addition Study (ERAS)
summary: FERC-approved temporary fast track for generation interconnection; first requests Aug 2025. A generation pathway, not a load queue.

name: MISO, LMR and demand response enrollment FAQ
summary: Minimums: LMR 0.1 MW, DRR 1 MW, EDR 0.1 MW. 2 to 6 hour notice, events up to 4 hours, up to 16 dispatches a year. Enrollment tool opens 1 Dec 2026; no API.

name: EIA-411 Coordinated Bulk Power Supply and Demand Program
summary: Planners' capacity, demand and growth estimates by NERC assessment area. Geography changed in 2011.

name: EIA-860M monthly generator inventory (API)
summary: Monthly generator-level operating status and capacity via EIA API v2.

name: EIA Open Data API v2
summary: JSON/CSV API for EIA series including EIA-930 hourly grid data (from 2019). Free key.

name: EIA state electricity data
summary: State-level capacity, generation, sales and related historical series.

name: EIA Energy Atlas, Electric Power Transmission Lines
summary: Transmission line GIS layer. Research could not retrieve metadata; an older EIA layer is archived. HIFLD legacy portal returned not-found. Check before relying on it.

name: EIA, wholesale electricity markets overview
summary: Map and links for each US ISO/RTO region.

name: DOE, National Transmission Needs Study
summary: Current and future transmission constraints as demand rises; most modeled congestion falls in a small fraction of hours.

name: DOE, Electricity Rate Designs for Large Loads (2025)
summary: Utility and regulatory treatment of large new loads: cost allocation and rate design.

name: DOE i2X, DER Interconnection Roadmap (2025)
summary: Distribution DER interconnection under 100 kV / 80 MW. 2030 targets: under 75 days for 50 kW to 5 MW, under 140 days above 5 MW. Aspirational, not legal deadlines.

name: DOE, Distribution Grid Code Adoption Pathways (2024)
summary: Taxonomy of grid codes; hosting capacity publication choices and five validation stages.

name: DOE, The Future of Resource Adequacy (2024)
summary: Explains nameplate vs capacity credit: equal MW is not equal reliability. Covers DR, DERMS, ADMS, VPPs.

name: FERC, Energy Primer (2024 edition)
summary: Staff handbook on electricity and gas markets; RTO/ISO sections for PJM, MISO, CAISO. Vocabulary, not tariff.

name: LBNL / DOE, Data Center Load Flexibility Workshop Summary (2025)
summary: Nov 2024 workshop, 49 participants: workload shifting, storage, onsite generation, demand response, communications and control needs.

name: LBNL, Integrating AI Data Centers with the Power Grid (2026)
summary: Four flexibility mechanisms: temporal/geographic compute shifting, facility infrastructure flexibility, storage, onsite generation.

name: EPRI DCFlex deliverables (load shape library and reports)
summary: Data center load shape library (first edition 2025), storage assessments, flexible design and program mappings.

name: EPRI Flex MOSAIC
summary: Framework classifying data center flexibility by response characteristics across workloads, generation, storage and cooling.

name: EPRI DCFlex Workstream 2: Programs
summary: Maps US and European utility programs and market services to EPRI flexibility classes.

name: EPRI DCFlex demonstrations
summary: At least ten planned demos (Phoenix, Lenoir, Paris, Chicago named): AI workload modulation, DR, backup integration, ride-through. Page does not give curtailment MW.

name: Google Cloud, Using demand response to reduce data center power consumption (2023)
summary: Grid event notices feed Google's compute planner, which sets hourly limits on non-urgent tasks per site (delay or reroute). Europe, Taiwan, US examples. No MW series published.

name: Google Cloud, Mitigating power and thermal fluctuations in ML infrastructure (2025)
summary: Synchronized ML clusters swing tens of MW every few seconds; compiler-level smoothing cut swings about 50% with under 1% performance loss and slightly higher average power.

name: LBNL / CPUC, California Demand Response Potential Study Phase 4 (2024)
summary: Shed and shift DR potential in California through 2050 by end use.

name: SustainDC (HPE dc-rl)
creator: Hewlett Packard Enterprise
summary: Multi-agent RL environments for data center workload shifting, HVAC setpoints and batteries with carbon, weather and Alibaba/Google workload inputs. Metrics: energy, carbon, water, dropped tasks. Mixed MIT / CC BY-NC.

name: HELICS co-simulation framework
creator: US DOE Grid Modernization Lab Consortium (PNNL, LLNL, NREL)
summary: Couples separate simulators (grid, buildings, markets, comms) into one time-synchronized federation. Python bindings. Simulates nothing on its own. BSD-3.

name: EnergyPlus (now under NatLabRockies)
creator: US DOE, NREL (now NLR)
summary: Whole-building energy and HVAC simulation with Python API. Needs facility inputs; not a calibrated data center model out of the box.

name: Scaphandre
creator: Hubblo
summary: Rust agent reporting host and VM power, exporting to Prometheus, JSON and others. Early-stage. Apache-2.0.

name: PowerAPI
creator: Inria and University of Lille
summary: Python framework for software-defined power meters down to process level. Estimates, not physical metering. BSD-3.

name: Azure LLM inference traces 2023, 2024 and multimodal 2025
summary: Production request traces: timestamp, context tokens, generated tokens (plus images in the 2025 multimodal trace). No power, location or deadlines. CC BY.

name: CAISO Demand Response participation
summary: Proxy Demand Resource and Reliability DR Resource models. Needs a scheduling coordinator and revenue-quality meters; ancillary services need telemetry.

name: CAISO Distributed Energy Resource Provider model
summary: DER aggregations in wholesale markets. Utility concurrence review of 30 business days, then onboarding, metering and agreements.

name: CAISO, Demand and Distributed Energy Market Integration straw proposal (Mar 2026)
summary: Stakeholder initiative on market pathways for large flexible loads and DER aggregations.

name: CAISO DMM, Demand Response Issues and Performance 2025
summary: 2025 demand response activity and performance across CAISO and WEIM.

name: CAISO DMM, Demand Response Issues and Performance 2024
summary: DR was about 1,400 MW, 2.6% of CAISO RA capacity in summer 2024; only 44% of utility PDR RA capacity was bid on high-load days.

name: PG&E Rule 24 (third-party demand response)
summary: Customers enroll with third-party DR providers that bid aggregated reductions into CAISO.

name: PG&E business demand response programs (incl. Capacity Bidding)
summary: Capacity Bidding Program and other business DR offerings with incentives and performance obligations.

name: SCE Capacity Bidding Program Elect
summary: Pays participants for temporary reductions during high demand; overlap restrictions with other DR programs.

name: SCE Emergency Load Reduction Program
summary: Seven-year DR pilot 2021 to 2027 for qualifying non-residential customers, including CCA and Direct Access.

name: California Demand Side Grid Support (DSGS) program
summary: Pays eligible customers for net load reduction and backup generation during extreme events, May to October. Fifth Edition guidelines adopted 27 Apr 2026.

name: CEC docket 22-RENEW-01 (DSGS data and guidelines)
summary: Includes anonymized 2024 and 2025 storage VPP performance workbooks (monthly site and hourly discharge), enrolled capacity by county. Measured distributed storage, not compute.

name: DOE, VPP Liftoff update announcement (Jan 2025)
summary: 33 GW of VPPs in North America; 80 to 160 GW by 2030 scenario (10% to 20% of peak).

name: DOE, Distribution Grid Orchestration (Nov 2024)
summary: Taxonomy of DER orchestration: dispatch-signal, autonomous, behavioral; local feeder constraints vs grid-wide signals; OpenADR and IEEE 2030.5 roles.

name: DOE, Sourcing DER for Distribution Services (2024)
summary: How utilities procure DER for local distribution needs, distinct from wholesale aggregation.

name: PG&E EPIC 3.11, Redwood Coast Airport Microgrid final report (2024)
summary: Measured community microgrid: 2.3 MW / 8.8 MWh battery plus 2.2 MW PV; 51+ hours of resilience across 12 events; fixed limited interconnection avoided reconductoring.

name: EnergyHub edge DERMS utility integrations
summary: Commercial DERMS integration gateway, including GE Vernova GridOS. No public API or sandbox.

name: GRIDAPPS-D IEEE 2030.5 repositories
creator: PNNL (GridAPPS-D)
summary: Go components for IEEE 2030.5 server, client and inverter simulator. Repository existence only; conformance not checked.

name: FERC Order No. 2222 fact sheet
summary: Minimum aggregation size in RTO/ISO markets may be no greater than 100 kW.

name: AINETUS
creator: LF Energy community
summary: AI for Safety-Critical Network Infrastructures: human-centric AI components that support grid operators' real-time and planning decisions. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/ainetus.

name: Arras (formerly HiPAS GridLAB-D)
creator: LF Energy; GridLAB-D originally developed by PNNL for US DOE
summary: Grid and smart-grid simulation for utilities and researchers, the continuation of HiPAS GridLAB-D. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/arras-energy/gridlabd.

name: AssetLife
creator: RTE (France)
summary: Python library for asset management: survival analysis, renewal theory and cost calculation for maintenance and replacement decisions. Apache-2.0. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/AssetLife-project.

name: Battery Data Alliance
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Common software and data schemas for battery data across companies. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/battery-data-alliance.

name: CDS Customer Data
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Open specifications for access to utility customer energy data, for carbon accounting, efficiency and flexibility use cases. Code: github.com/lfe-cds/CDS-Customer-Data.

name: CDS Power Systems Data
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Open specification for raw power system data, aimed at more accurate grid emissions reporting. Code: github.com/lfe-cds/CDS-Power-Systems-Data.

name: CDS Registration
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Open specifications for how third-party systems securely discover, register with and connect to utility platforms. Code: github.com/lfe-cds/CDS-Registration.

name: CitrineOS
creator: S44 Energy
summary: Open-source charger network management software for OCPP 2.0.1: monitor, control and manage charging stations. Code: github.com/citrineos/citrineos.

name: CoMPAS
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Shared software blocks for IEC 61850 profile configuration in digital substations. LF Energy stage: Early Adoption. Code: github.com/com-pas.

name: covXtreme
creator: Shell
summary: Statistical modelling of extreme values and how they occur together, for risk from rare severe conditions. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/covXtreme.

name: CUPID
creator: LF Energy; from the Horizon Europe InterSTORE project
summary: Interoperability toolkit that extends IEEE 2030.5 for distributed energy resources and energy management systems. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/cupid-project.

name: Dynawo
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Simulation suite for power system dynamics: voltage, frequency, short circuit and stability with power-electronic resources and HVDC. Code: github.com/dynawo.

name: EnerGNN
creator: RTE with University of Liège and partners
summary: Graph neural network stack (H2MG) for amortized optimization: trained once on many grid cases, it returns near-instant solutions to new ones. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/energnn/energnn.

name: FIDOpower
creator: SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory
summary: Notebook-based tools for reproducible power system analysis. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/fidopower.

name: FlexMeasures
creator: Seita Energy Flexibility (Nicolas Höning)
summary: Open-source energy optimization engine that forecasts and schedules flexible loads, batteries and generation against prices and grid limits, for real-time operations. Built by Seita (https://seita.nl/), founded by Nicolas Höning; hosted by LF Energy. LF Energy stage: Incubation. Code: github.com/FlexMeasures/flexmeasures (Apache-2.0).

name: GEISA (Grid Edge Interoperability & Security Alliance)
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Secure, interoperable ecosystem for deploying and operating grid edge computing and applications. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/geisa.

name: GridVantage
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Agent-based grid modelling with resilience metrics to help operators prepare for and recover from extreme weather. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/grid-vantage.

name: Hyphae
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Microgrid software connecting buildings, homes and devices to local generation, storage and EV batteries. LF Energy stage: Incubation. Code: github.com/hyphae.

name: NODE Collective
creator: Building Decarbonization Coalition, Rewiring America, Eli Technologies
summary: National open database of US electrification incentives and rebates. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/NODE-Collective.

name: OpenDSM (formerly OpenEEmeter)
creator: Recurve
summary: Measures savings and demand-side impact from meter data, for programs that need verified results. Code: github.com/opendsm/opendsm.

name: OpenGridFM
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Open framework for building and fine-tuning foundation models for power grids. LF Energy stage: Incubation. Code: github.com/gridfm.

name: OpenSTEF
creator: LF Energy community (grid operators, vendors, researchers)
summary: Python machine learning pipelines for short-term energy forecasts. LF Energy stage: Incubation. Code: github.com/OpenSTEF/openstef.

name: OpenSynth
creator: Centre for Net Zero
summary: Open data community for synthetic and real energy datasets, starting with demand. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/OpenSynth-energy.

name: OperatorFabric
creator: RTE (France)
summary: Control-room platform that brings alerts, workflows and messages from many systems into one interface. MPL-2.0. LF Energy stage: Early Adoption. Code: github.com/opfab.

name: ORES: Open Renewable Energy Systems
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Open standards and practice for plug-and-play microgrids and grid-interactive device metadata and APIs. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/open-renewable-energy-systems.

name: p-SWAMP
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Modular research environment for wide-area monitoring and protection with simulation. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/p-swamp/P-SWAMP.

name: Power Grid Model
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Fast calculation engine for distribution grids: power flow, state estimation and short circuit. LF Energy stage: Early Adoption. Code: github.com/PowerGridModel.

name: PowSyBl
creator: RTE (France)
summary: Library and tools for power system modelling: load flow, security analysis, dynamic simulation, many grid formats. MPL-2.0. LF Energy stage: Early Adoption. Code: github.com/powsybl.

name: RTDIP: Real Time Data Ingestion Platform
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Cloud pipelines for ingesting and querying real-time and historical time-series data. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/rtdip.

name: RTC-Tools
creator: Deltares
summary: Toolbox for control and optimization of time-dependent systems, originally water systems; MESIDO extends it to energy networks. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/Multi-Energy-Systems-Optimization/mesido.

name: SEAPATH
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Real-time platform that runs IEC 61850 substation protection and control as virtual machines or containers on standard servers. LF Energy stage: Graduated. Code: github.com/seapath.

name: Semantic Energy Framework (SEF)
creator: LF Energy; from the EU InterConnect project
summary: Semantic interoperability so energy apps and devices interpret shared data the same way. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/lfe-sef.

name: Shapeshifter
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Implements the USEF Flexibility Trading Protocol for coordinating flexibility between grid operators and aggregators. LF Energy stage: Incubation. Code: github.com/shapeshifter.

name: Smart HEMS Benchmark
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Manufacturer-neutral benchmark for home energy management systems with solar and batteries. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/SMART-HEMS-Benchmark/smart-hems-benchmark.

name: SOGNO
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Modular, cloud-native automation for distribution utilities: monitoring, state estimation and control. LF Energy stage: Early Adoption. Code: github.com/sogno-platform.

name: TROLIE
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Open specification for exchanging current and forecast transmission line ratings, as required by FERC Order 881. Apache-2.0. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/trolie/spec.

name: Utility Rate Plan Exchange (URPX)
creator: Flux Tailor with the National Laboratory of the Rockies
summary: Open, machine-readable standard for utility tariffs and rate plans. Apache-2.0. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/urpx-org.

name: VAREN
creator: LF Energy community
summary: Python library that automates analysis of mobile LiDAR of overhead distribution lines and nearby vegetation. LF Energy stage: Sandbox. Code: github.com/varen-project.

name: Weco AI, AIDE2: outer-loop agent rewrites an inner-loop research agent (2026)
summary: Reports an outer agent improving the code of an inner research agent, with gains carrying to unseen domains. Preprint, Sept 2026.

name: Zhang et al., Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents (2025)
summary: Coding agent rewrites its own code; archive-based open-ended search raised SWE-bench and Polyglot scores.

name: Hyperagents (DGM-H), 2026
summary: Self-referential agents that can also edit their improvement procedure; reports gains outside coding.

name: Novikov et al., AlphaEvolve (Google DeepMind, 2025)
summary: LLM-driven evolutionary coding agent with automated evaluators; reported results in math, scheduling and kernel optimization.

name: Romera-Paredes et al., Mathematical discoveries from program search with LLMs (Nature 2023)
summary: FunSearch: LLM proposes programs, evaluator scores them, best are recycled into prompts. New cap set constructions.

name: Zelikman et al., Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP) (2023)
summary: A scaffolding program that improves code is applied to improving itself. Early recursive scaffolding result.

name: Robeyns et al., A Self-Improving Coding Agent (2025)
summary: Agent edits its own codebase between benchmark runs and keeps edits that raise scores.

name: Shinn et al., Reflexion (2023)
summary: Agents store verbal feedback from failed attempts in memory and use it on the next try, without weight updates.

name: Wang et al., Voyager (2023)
summary: LLM agent builds a growing library of verified code skills through self-verification.

name: Agrawal et al., GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution (2025)
summary: Prompt optimization by reflecting on traces; reports outperforming RL fine-tuning (GRPO) with fewer rollouts.

name: Lu et al., The AI Scientist (2024)
summary: Automated pipeline for idea generation, experiments, paper writing and automated review.

name: AutoLab: long-horizon closed-loop optimization benchmark (2026)
summary: 36 expert tasks across system optimization, model development and CUDA kernels. Finds sustained iteration matters more than first attempt.

name: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey (2026)
summary: Survey organizing self-improvement by which component changes (prompt, memory, tools, code, weights).

name: Shehabi et al., 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report (LBNL)
summary: US data centers used 176 TWh, about 4.4% of US electricity, in 2023; 325 to 580 TWh (6.7% to 12%) projected for 2028. Bottom-up equipment model. Superseded by lbnl-dc-energy-2025-update for 2030.

name: IEA, Energy and AI (2025)
summary: Global data centers used 415 TWh in 2024 (about 1.5%); 945 TWh in 2030 base case. US and China are nearly 80% of growth. Data centers build in 2 to 3 years, grid infrastructure takes longer. CC BY 4.0.

name: EPRI, Powering Intelligence (2024)
summary: Scenarios of US data center load growth to 2030 with state-level breakdown.

name: Norris et al., Rethinking Load Growth (Duke Nicholas Institute, 2025)
summary: First-order study of the 22 largest balancing authorities: nearly 100 GW of new load could use existing capacity if it accepts limited curtailment during grid stress.

name: Radovanovic et al., Carbon-Aware Computing for Datacenters (Google, 2021)
summary: Google's system that shifts flexible compute in time using day-ahead carbon forecasts and cluster-level virtual capacity curves.

name: Colangelo et al., Turning AI Data Centers into Grid-Interactive Assets (2025)
summary: Field demo in Phoenix: software-only control cut an AI cluster's power by 25% for 3 hours during a grid peak event.

name: Severson et al., Data-driven prediction of battery cycle life before capacity degradation (Nature Energy 2019)
summary: Predicts cycle life from the first 100 cycles. Dataset is data.matr.io (see matr-battery).

name: Attia et al., Closed-loop optimization of fast-charging protocols (Nature 2020)
summary: Bayesian optimization plus early cycle-life prediction found long-life fast-charge protocols in 16 days instead of an estimated 500.

name: Merchant et al., Scaling deep learning for materials discovery (Nature 2023)
summary: GNoME: active learning loop of GNN prediction and DFT verification; reports 2.2M new crystals, 381k on the convex hull.

name: Szymanski et al., An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of novel materials (Nature 2023)
summary: Robotic lab with computational targets and active learning; 41 of 58 targets synthesized in 17 days. Claims later disputed in the literature.

name: Zeni et al., A generative model for inorganic materials design (Nature 2025)
summary: MatterGen diffusion model for property-conditioned crystal generation, with one generated material synthesized.

name: Chanussot et al., Open Catalyst 2020 (OC20) dataset and community challenges (2020)
summary: 1.2M DFT relaxations of adsorbates on catalyst surfaces with defined tasks and metrics.

name: Degrave et al., Magnetic control of tokamak plasmas through deep RL (Nature 2022)
summary: RL controller trained in simulation and run on the TCV tokamak to shape plasmas.

name: Seo et al., Avoiding fusion plasma tearing instability with deep RL (Nature 2024)
summary: RL controller on DIII-D that anticipates and avoids tearing instabilities in real time.

name: Citrin et al., TORAX: a fast and differentiable tokamak transport simulator in JAX (2024)
summary: Describes TORAX design, validation and use for optimization and control.

name: Babaeinejadsarookolaee et al., The Power Grid Library for Benchmarking AC OPF Algorithms (2019)
summary: Defines the PGLib-OPF benchmark cases and their intended use.

name: Price and Goodin, Reduced Network Modeling of WECC as a Market Design Prototype (IEEE PES 2011)
summary: Describes a 240-bus reduced Western Interconnection model built by CAISO staff, detailed inside California, with hourly load profiles for CAISO areas. Paywalled; the case file is not bundled with MATPOWER.

name: NVIDIA, Omniverse DSX Blueprint for gigawatt-scale AI factories (Oct 2025)
summary: Announces DSX Boost (power-optimized operation), DSX Flex (demand matched to real-time grid conditions with AI agents from Emerald AI and Phaidra) and DSX Exchange. NVIDIA claims DSX Flex can help tap some of 100 GW of underused grid capacity (vendor claim).

name: EPRI DCFlex
summary: EPRI initiative with utilities, operators and hyperscalers to demonstrate data center flexibility at field sites.

name: FERC Order No. 2222
summary: Requires RTOs/ISOs to let DER aggregations into energy, capacity and ancillary markets; minimum aggregation size no more than 100 kW. Does not apply to ERCOT. Implementation dates on the page are as of Aug 2024.

name: Texas SB 6 (89th Legislature, 2025): large load rules in ERCOT
summary: Texas law on interconnection standards and grid-emergency curtailment for large loads such as data centers. Read the enrolled text for thresholds.

name: Google, data center demand response agreements with utilities (2025)
summary: Aug 2025: agreements with Indiana Michigan Power and TVA to reduce ML workload power during grid events, after three OPPD events in 2024. Google calls it early-stage and location-limited. No MW, payments or event caps disclosed.

name: OpenADR 3.0
summary: REST/OpenAPI standard for DR, price and DER signals; public YAML spec supplements 2.0a/b. Reference implementation is members-only; certification is separate from implementing the API.

name: IEEE 2030.5-2023 Smart Energy Profile
summary: Application protocol for utility communication with DERs; required for inverter communication under California Rule 21.

name: IEEE 1547-2018
summary: Interconnection and interoperability standard for DERs connected to distribution grids.

name: FERC Critical Energy/Electric Infrastructure Information (CEII)
summary: Rules restricting detailed grid data such as real network models; access requires a request and non-disclosure agreement. The reason public studies rely on synthetic grids.

name: OCPP: Open Charge Point Protocol (Open Charge Alliance)
summary: Open protocol between EV chargers and charging management systems, including smart charging profiles that cap or schedule charging power.

name: ISO 15118-20: vehicle to grid communication interface
summary: Standard for communication between vehicle and charger, adding bidirectional power transfer to plug and charge and scheduling. Paid standard.

name: CPUC transportation electrification
summary: California utility EV programs, rates and rulemakings, including vehicle-grid integration.

name: SunSpec specifications and certification
summary: SunSpec Alliance specifications for DER communication (SunSpec Modbus, IEEE 2030.5/CSIP test specs, security). Certification programs and test labs: https://sunspec.org/certifications/.

name: AIDE (Weco AI)
creator: Weco AI
summary: Agent that iterates on ML code with a tree search over solutions, scored by a user-defined metric.

name: autoresearch (Andrej Karpathy)
creator: Andrej Karpathy
summary: Minimal loop where an agent edits a training script, runs a short experiment, and keeps changes that improve a validation metric.

name: OpenEvolve
creator: Asankhaya Sharma
summary: Open-source implementation of the AlphaEvolve pattern: an LLM mutates programs and an evaluator scores them across generations.

name: ShinkaEvolve (Sakana AI)
creator: Sakana AI
summary: Sample-efficient LLM-driven program evolution framework with novelty filtering and an archive of solutions.

name: Darwin Godel Machine
creator: Jenny Zhang et al. (UBC, Sakana AI)
summary: Coding agent that edits its own code and keeps an archive of agent variants, scored on coding benchmarks.

name: FunSearch (Google DeepMind)
creator: Google DeepMind
summary: LLM proposes programs, an automated evaluator scores them, best programs are fed back. Released code for the Nature 2023 paper.

name: DSPy
creator: Stanford NLP
summary: Framework that optimizes LLM prompts and pipelines against a metric instead of hand-written prompts.

name: GEPA
creator: Lakshya A. Agrawal et al.
summary: Reflective prompt evolution: an LLM reads execution traces and rewrites prompts, keeping a Pareto set of candidates.

name: The AI Scientist (Sakana AI)
creator: Sakana AI
summary: End-to-end loop that generates research ideas, runs experiments from templates and writes papers.

name: MLE-bench (OpenAI)
creator: OpenAI
summary: 75 Kaggle competitions used to measure how well agents do ML engineering.

name: gridstatus (Python library)
creator: Grid Status
summary: Python API for load, prices, fuel mix and queue data from US ISOs (CAISO, ERCOT, PJM, MISO, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE).

name: Inframation (inframation.io): map of the energy buildout (FREE BETA)
creator: Compass International
license: Free beta, not open source; no site license yet, each record carries its source's license
summary: Free while in beta, per https://inframation.io/pricing. Searchable map of planned, under-construction, operating and retired power plants, batteries, data centers, large loads, lines and substations in the US and GB, plus energy RFPs and funding, built from interconnection queues, EIA-860M and permit registers with every record linked to its source. Includes a site finder (land near high-voltage lines and substations, out of the floodplain), free RSS/JSON feeds and a keyless public API at https://api.inframation.io.

name: Electricity Maps API
summary: Zone-level carbon intensity, mix, flows, load and day-ahead prices: latest, history and forecast; 5 min to hourly. Lifecycle and flow-traced by default, not marginal. 14-day trial.

name: WattTime API
summary: Signals: co2_moer (marginal, lb/MWh), co2_aoer (average), health_damage (USD/MWh), with forecasts for load shifting. API docs could not be fetched in research; check access terms.

name: Carbon Aware SDK (Green Software Foundation)
creator: Green Software Foundation
summary: Web API and CLI that wrap carbon intensity providers and return the best time and location to run a workload.

name: Kepler (Kubernetes power exporter)
creator: Sustainable Computing community (CNCF)
summary: Exports estimated power use per Kubernetes pod and container as Prometheus metrics.

name: Vessim
creator: TU Berlin (DOS group)
summary: Co-simulation testbed for computing systems with solar, batteries and grid signals. Built for carbon-aware computing experiments.

name: REopt (NREL, now NLR)
creator: NREL (now NLR)
summary: Optimizes the size and dispatch of on-site solar, storage and generators for a site's load and tariff. Julia package and web API.

name: System Advisor Model (SAM, NREL, now NLR)
creator: NREL (now NLR)
summary: Performance and financial models for solar, wind, storage and other systems. Python access through PySAM.

name: reV (Renewable Energy Potential model, NREL, now NLR)
creator: NREL (now NLR)
summary: Geospatial model of renewable generation potential, supply curves and siting exclusions.

name: OpenLEADR (OpenADR 2.0b in Python)
creator: LF Energy (OpenLEADR)
summary: LF Energy project with open-source OpenADR implementations: openleadr-python (OpenADR 2.0b VEN and VTN, developmental) and openleadr-rs (Rust, OpenADR 3). Code: github.com/openleadr.

name: pymatgen
creator: Materials Project (LBNL)
summary: Python library for crystal structures, phase diagrams, electrochemistry analysis and Materials Project access.

name: Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE)
creator: ASE community (DTU)
summary: Python toolkit to set up, run and analyze atomistic simulations with many calculators, including ML potentials.

name: MACE
creator: ACEsuit (University of Cambridge and others)
summary: Machine-learned interatomic potentials, including foundation models (MACE-MP) that run near-DFT checks in seconds.

name: CHGNet
creator: Ceder Group (UC Berkeley)
summary: Universal ML potential trained on Materials Project trajectories, includes magnetic moments. Runs on CPU or GPU.

name: MatterSim (Microsoft)
creator: Microsoft Research
summary: Universal ML potential for materials across elements, temperatures and pressures.

name: Orb models (Orbital Materials)
creator: Orbital Materials
summary: Pretrained universal ML interatomic potentials with ASE calculator interface.

name: fairchem (Meta FAIR Chemistry)
creator: Meta FAIR Chemistry
summary: Models and tooling for Open Catalyst and OMat datasets, including pretrained potentials for catalysts and materials.

name: MatterGen (Microsoft)
creator: Microsoft Research
summary: Diffusion model that generates crystal structures conditioned on target properties.

name: Matbench Discovery
creator: Materials Project (LBNL)
summary: Leaderboard ranking ML models on predicting stability of new crystals.

name: PyBaMM
creator: PyBaMM team (University of Oxford and others)
summary: Python battery models (SPM, SPMe, DFN) with degradation submodels and parameter sets. Simulates a cycling protocol in seconds.

name: Grid2Op (RTE France)
creator: RTE France, hosted by LF Energy
summary: Power grid operation environment for RL and agents, used in the L2RPN competitions. Agents act on topology and redispatch.

name: pandapower
creator: Fraunhofer IEE and University of Kassel
summary: Python power flow and optimal power flow on pandas tables, with standard test networks.

name: PyPSA
creator: PyPSA team
summary: Python power system optimization: capacity expansion, unit commitment and power flow.

name: PyPSA-USA
creator: PyPSA-USA contributors
summary: Open US power system model built on PyPSA with EIA and other public data.

name: PGLib-OPF
creator: IEEE PES Task Force on OPF benchmarks
summary: Standard benchmark library of optimal power flow test cases from 3 to 30,000 buses.

name: MATPOWER
creator: MATPOWER team (Ray Zimmerman)
summary: MATLAB/Octave power flow and OPF package. Its case format is used by most grid benchmarks.

name: PowerModels.jl
creator: Los Alamos National Laboratory
summary: Julia package for steady-state power network optimization with many formulations.

name: OpenDSSDirect.py
creator: DSS-Extensions (OpenDSS by EPRI)
summary: Python bindings for OpenDSS distribution system simulator. Used for feeder-level hosting capacity studies.

name: GridLAB-D
creator: PNNL
summary: Distribution system and end-use load simulator from PNNL, including responsive loads and markets.

name: CityLearn
creator: Intelligent Environments Lab (UT Austin), hosted by LF Energy
summary: Gym environment for coordinated demand response of many buildings with storage and solar.

name: BuildingsBench (NREL, now NLR)
creator: NREL (now NLR)
summary: Benchmark and 900k simulated buildings for short-term load forecasting, including zero-shot tests on real buildings.

name: TORAX (Google DeepMind)
creator: Google DeepMind
summary: Differentiable tokamak core transport simulator in JAX. Fast enough to run inside optimization loops.

name: FreeGS
creator: FreeGS contributors (Ben Dudson)
summary: Free-boundary Grad-Shafranov plasma equilibrium solver in Python.

name: FreeGSNKE
creator: FusionComputingLab (UKAEA, STFC Hartree Centre)
summary: Evolutive free-boundary equilibrium solver built on FreeGS, for time-dependent tokamak simulation.

name: Open FUSION Toolkit
creator: Open FUSION Toolkit team
summary: Finite element codes for plasma equilibrium (TokaMaker), MHD and 3D wall eddy currents.

name: PlasmaPy
creator: PlasmaPy community
summary: Community Python package for plasma physics formulary and analysis.

name: Google Solar API
summary: Per-building roof area, panel layouts, sunshine hours and estimated yearly solar output. Needs a Google Cloud project with billing and an API key.

name: Google Earth Engine
summary: Cloud catalogue and compute for satellite imagery and geospatial datasets (Landsat, Sentinel, NAIP, land cover, ERA5). Free for non-commercial use after registering a Cloud project; Python and JavaScript APIs.

name: surge: open probabilistic day-ahead US load forecasts
creator: Tyler Gibbs
summary: Day-ahead probabilistic load forecasts for all 53 US balancing authorities: Chronos-2 fine-tuned on seven years of EIA-930 data. MIT.

name: OpenEAC Alliance M&V methodologies
creator: OpenEAC Alliance (repo maintained by WattCarbon)
summary: Open, peer-reviewed measurement and verification (M&V) methodologies for issuing Energy Attribute Certificates (EACs) per watt-hour or gram CO2e from battery storage, electrification, demand response and energy efficiency projects. Methods and statuses at methods.openeac.org; drafts go through a 30-day public comment period.

name: pvlib-python
creator: pvlib community (Sandia origin)
summary: Python functions for solar position, irradiance, PV cell temperature and DC/AC output. The standard open PV performance model. BSD-3.

name: Solar-Forecasting: physics-based smart persistence model (NREL, now NLR)
creator: NREL (now NLR)
summary: NREL software record SWR-18-36: physics-based smart persistence model for intra-hour solar forecasting. BSD-3. Last updated 2022.

name: GridSFM: small foundation models for the power grid (Microsoft Research)
creator: Microsoft Research
summary: Microsoft Research framework for small foundation models in grid optimization, starting with AC optimal power flow. Learns from graph representations of topology, load, dispatch, flows and voltages across many scenarios. Open checkpoint (GridSFM_Open), datasets on Hugging Face, and an open-data pipeline from OpenStreetMap to solved OPF cases. Suited to fast screening (contingencies, planning scenarios, new data center load) and to giving exact solvers a starting point, not replacing them. MIT.

name: TimeCopilot: agentic forecasting framework
creator: TimeCopilot
summary: LLM agent over time-series foundation models: forecast, cross-validate and detect anomalies from natural-language requests through one API. MIT.

name: Nixtla TimeGPT SDK
summary: Python SDK for TimeGPT, a pre-trained time-series foundation model for forecasting and anomaly detection, including electricity. Needs a Nixtla API key.

name: Coral NPU (Google)
creator: Google
summary: Open machine learning accelerator core designed for energy-efficient AI at the edge. Hardware design, Apache-2.0.

name: NILMTK: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring Toolkit
creator: NILMTK community
summary: Toolkit to disaggregate a whole-building meter into appliance loads, with loaders for public datasets including the US REDD dataset. Apache-2.0.

name: Open Sustainable Technology directory
summary: Directory and analysis of open-source projects in climate, sustainable energy and natural resources. Use it to find more tools. CC BY 4.0.

name: Load Flow Simulator (browser)
creator: Adjie Brotosukmono
summary: Free browser tool: draw a single-line diagram and run AC Newton-Raphson or DC load flow (PyPSA-based), with animated flows. Examples include a 9-bus system, a 20/0.4 kV feeder and an HVDC link. Offers a link for AI agents to open a scenario.

name: ED/UC Simulator: economic dispatch and unit commitment (browser)
creator: Adjie Brotosukmono
summary: Free browser tool: draw a network, decide which units run hour by hour and read nodal prices (LMP); PyPSA with the HiGHS solver. Examples include a PJM 5-bus case and solar plus battery.

name: Generic EMT Modeling of Data Center Load (Dartmouth)
creator: Xingyu Zhao, Yingyi Tang, Junbo Zhao (Dartmouth)
summary: Modular electromagnetic transient model of a data center fed by a centralized UPS: rectifier, inverter, battery DC-DC, PFC, buck and VFD modules at three fidelity levels, IT load profiles and voltage ride-through control. Needs PSCAD 5.0.2 (commercial). No license file in the repo; ask the authors before reusing code.

name: ANDES: power system transient dynamics in Python (CURENT)
creator: CURENT (Hantao Cui et al.)
summary: Python library for phasor-domain transient stability simulation with symbolic model definitions, including inverter-based resource models. See the repo for license.

name: acnportal / ACN-Sim (Caltech)
creator: Caltech (Zach Lee, Steven Low group)
summary: Simulator for scheduling many EV chargers under site capacity limits, plus a client for ACN-Data. BSD-3.

name: EVerest: open-source EV charging software stack (LF Energy)
creator: PIONIX GmbH, hosted by LF Energy
summary: Charger firmware and software stack implementing OCPP and ISO 15118 for EV charging stations. Apache-2.0.

name: EVI-X toolbox (NREL, now NLR)
creator: NREL (now NLR)
summary: Models for EV charging demand and infrastructure needs (EVI-Pro family), with web versions.

name: Manta: open energy system modelling platform
creator: Open Energy Transition
summary: Open-source application for energy system modelling with graphical no-code workflows and full customization; plug-ins for PyPSA, GenX, Sienna and other frameworks; runs in the cloud, locally or on-premise; AI-assisted setup, debugging and results exploration. Code: github.com/manta-plan/manta (Apache-2.0). Launched 2026; public roadmap and beta program.

name: GenX capacity expansion model (MIT, Princeton)
creator: MIT and Princeton (GenX team)
summary: Julia model that chooses which generation, storage and transmission to build and how to operate it, for low-carbon power system studies. GPL-2.0. Needs Julia and a solver.

name: AC Grid Lab (browser AC power flow)
creator: Dr. Eshan Singh
summary: Browser tool: build a one-line network on a map or diagram and solve AC power flow; starter case is a California-inspired nine-bus network with voltage and line-loading checks. JSON import and export.

name: NRGISE Open: local energy system simulator
creator: Fraunhofer ISE (Tobias Rohrer, Nils Reiners, Ricarda Hogl)
summary: Python time-step simulation of local energy systems (PV, storage, loads) with control strategies: peak shaving, self-consumption, controller benchmarking, forecast-error studies, batch sweeps. pip install nrgise. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial).

name: Flexible BESS dispatch and arbitrage optimizer under grid constraints
creator: Mohammadreza Refaei
summary: Optimizes battery charging and discharging across market prices while respecting hourly non-firm grid export limits and degradation cost. Example data from the German market. No clear license in the repo; ask before reusing code.

name: PyPSA California: interactive grid model (browser)
creator: Dr. Eshan Singh
summary: Browser app over a PyPSA optimization model of the California grid: configure demand, generation, storage, transmission and policy, then solve. No install.

name: flex-pse: industrial energy flexibility optimization (Stanford)
creator: Stanford
summary: Stanford open-source Pyomo/IDAES toolbox: model a facility as a time-discretized optimization, fit it from plant data, and schedule it against real electricity tariffs and demand response signals. pip install flex-pse. Apache-2.0. Community Slack: https://join.slack.com/t/flex-pse/shared_invite/zt-4b2va6ztg-K74JiAdHsmqY2CoGjbOmIQ

name: Satori: open IEEE 2030.5 and SunSpec Modbus reference implementations
creator: DER Security Corp (DERSec)
summary: IEEE 2030.5 / CSIP client with a SunSpec Modbus bridge that connects inverters, batteries and EVs to utility programs without firmware changes. pip install py20305; code at github.com/DERSecurity/py20305 (Apache-2.0). Satori Scout, the free iOS/Android reference app, handles device discovery, simulation and VPP connectivity (source under commercial license).

name: OpenIBR: open-source grid-forming controls
creator: Heron Power
summary: Universal grid-forming controller for inverter-based resources and large electronic loads such as data centers, aligned with IEEE 2800 and UNIFI. v1.1 builds IEEE/CIGRE TB958 DLLs from the open C code for PSCAD and similar tools, with debug outputs and a COMTRADE-logging test environment. Code: github.com/HeronPower/OpenIBR; DLL guide: github.com/HeronPower/OpenIBR/blob/dev/documentation/9_using_the_ieee_cigre_dll.md

name: Pravah: weather forecasting for the grid (India)
creator: Pravah team
summary: Weather forecasting built for power grid operations in India. Not public: access on request. Email arhams@stanford.edu for a contact.

name: NVIDIA Omniverse DSX Blueprint: digital twins of AI data centers
creator: NVIDIA
summary: Developer blueprint for OpenUSD digital twins of gigawatt-scale AI data centers: 50-acre reference site geometry, electrical loading and thermal (CFD) simulation, web viewer. DSX Flex matches facility demand to real-time grid conditions. Needs NVIDIA software and GPUs; NVIDIA says it is not turn-key for production.

name: NEPA MCP Toolkit (PermitAI, PNNL)
creator: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL)
summary: 23 Model Context Protocol servers that give AI agents federal environmental data for siting, NEPA review and permitting: permitting schedules, protected areas, species and critical habitat, wetlands, flood hazards, soils, air quality, cultural resources, Tribal lands, demographics, brownfields and federal regulations. pip install nepa-mcp; code at github.com/pnnl/nepa-mcp. Census and EPA AQS servers need free API keys.

name: py1815: open IEEE 1815 (DNP3) outstation
creator: DER Security Corp (DERSec), Project Satori
summary: The DNP3 (IEEE 1815) outstation of Project Satori, for distributed energy resources. Companion to the py20305 IEEE 2030.5 client.

name: pySunSpec2: SunSpec Modbus library
creator: SunSpec Alliance
summary: Python library for reading and controlling SunSpec Modbus devices such as inverters and batteries. Model definitions at github.com/sunspec/models. Used as the Modbus bridge in Project Satori.

name: SunSpec System Validation Platform (OpenSVP)
creator: SunSpec Alliance with CanmetENERGY-Varennes
summary: Open-source Python test platform and scripts for DER conformance testing against IEEE 1547.1, UL 1741 SA and AS/NZS 4777.2 with lab equipment or simulation.

name: EVSE Test System (QualityLogic)
creator: QualityLogic
summary: Modified EVerest stack for testing EV interoperability over DIN 70121 and ISO 15118-2, AC and DC: 20 conformance scenarios from CharIN and ChargeX specs, web dashboard, REST API, PCAP capture and software-in-the-loop mode without hardware.

name: QualityLogic IEEE 2030.5 test tools
creator: QualityLogic
summary: Commercial IEEE 2030.5 and CSIP test system for clients and servers, used as a certification test harness. Not open source.

name: Codibly IEEE 2030.5 Accelerator
creator: Codibly
summary: Pre-certified IEEE 2030.5 client and server code sold under a perpetual license with source. Codibly is a SunSpec authorized test lab for IEEE 2030.5 and CSIP. Not open source.
